text:
hector: Hey team, first-day question  I run `kubectl get ns` and get "You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized)". KUBECONFIG is ~/.kube/config. Who is the right contact for onboarding k8s access?

devops-bot: Welcome, Hector! :wave: Onboarding flow: `redwood-cli auth sso` then `redwood-cli kubeconfig fetch --env dev`. Docs: https://redwood.internal/onboarding/kubernetes. If the SSO popup is blocked use `--device-code`.

anika: hi! If your context still shows `minikube` after fetch, run `kubectl config use-context redwood-dev`. Also run `kubectl config current-context` to verify.

zane: default new hires get view on `default` + `platform-dev`. For other namespaces you need a request in #help or ask infra. Give GH handle and namespace names. For prod namespaces include `-prod` suffix.

hector: thanks. I have `redwood-dev` in contexts but `kubectl get pods -n ops` says forbidden (User "github|hector" cannot list resource "pods"). I guess RBAC.

caroline: yep. If it's onboarding-related we usually grant short-lived view (6-24h). Post your GH handle here and I'll grant 8h for ops. Also watch out for multiple kubeconfigs: `KUBECONFIG` merges them.

hector: GH `hectork`. Thanks Caroline.

caroline: granted view to `github|hectork` on `ops` for 8h. You should be able to `kubectl get pods -n ops` now.

zane: one extra tip: to avoid kubeconfig collisions I keep separate files and explicitly merge: `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/.kube/redwood kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/merged && export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/merged`.

hector: confirmed, can list pods now. Appreciate the quick help :tada:
